problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x=2\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,y=t+\frac{1}{t},\,t\in [1,e].
$$

Calculate the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.

feedback.problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x=6t-2{t}^{3},\,y=6{t}^{2},\,t\in [0,1].
$$

Determine the surface area $S$ generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis. Do not round the answer.

$S=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi y\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=0$ to ${t}_{2}=1.$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t-2{t}^{3})=6-6{t}^{2}, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2})=12t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}6{t}^{2}\sqrt{{(6-6{t}^{2})}^{2}+{(12t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}6{t}^{2}\sqrt{36-72{t}^{2}+36{t}^{4}+144{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}6{t}^{2}\sqrt{36{t}^{4}+72{t}^{2}+36}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, factoring the expression $36{t}^{4}+72{t}^{2}+36,$ we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}6{t}^{2}\sqrt{36({t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}6{t}^{2}\cdot 6\sqrt{{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =72\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{2}\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =72\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{2}\cdot |{t}^{2}+1|\,\text{d}t \\  & =72\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{2}({t}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =72\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{4}+{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =72\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{4}+{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =72\pi \cdot {[\frac{{t}^{5}}{5}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =72\pi [(\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{3})-(\frac{0}{5}+\frac{0}{3})] \\  & =72\pi \cdot \frac{8}{15} \\  & =\frac{192\pi }{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
